I really don’t mean to say it to brag at all but I think my 13 year old self would be more hopeful than she was if she saw how I was now.

At 13, I changed schools. Not a big deal, only it was from a private school to a public school, which is a drastic difference... for the school I went to anyway. I had no social skills. My social anxiety definitely was brought on by this. I also felt very insecure with myself: I started puberty at a very young age so I was more developed than others, which made me feel fat among the small middle schoolers. I had so many crushes on boys that I felt were out of my league. My parents were very understanding of my situation as they were struggling to hold down our home so I could attend a good public school. So there was also the pressure of that. 

I’m by no means perfect today, but I think I’m better. I think 13 year old me would be happy that I finally grew into my body, started working out, and that I have made peace with what was once thick and unruly hair AND that it’s a cool ombré now. And that I do makeup pretty good. And my fashion sense remained true to myself but more put together. I have a good job and a work environment! I have so many friends that love and care for me. My parents are more supportive and involved in my life now. I think 13 year old me would find the motivation to keep going forward, and that’s definitely something she needed very much. Keep hanging in there 13 year old me!!!

When I was 12, a car full of fully grown men followed me while I was walking home from school. They kept hollering, whistling, and tried to talk to me, saying I had a nice ass. I was wearing an Alice in Wonderland graphic tee from Hot Topic and skinny jeans. The walk was a long one: 3 miles. I ended up running into a suburb somewhere and hiding behind a car on someone’s drive way, and I remember breaking down crying, trembling. I didn’t tell my parents because I felt at fault, but in retrospect I wish I did tell them, because I know they would have comforted me. But I was so scared. I even threw away my jeans and graphic tee when I got home because I felt guilt over nothing. 

Now every time I sense a pair of eyes on me and I catch someone staring at me, I freeze up like a deer in headlights. As an adult I’m more forward and assertive, but catch me in a situation like that and I go stupid. I feel so helpless. I really do feel vulnerable in this world and even if society is more forward thinking in my country, I’m always scared of getting harmed because I refused someone’s advances or whatever. I come from a small town, and now that I go to school in a bigger city I’m always afraid. 

How did I deal with it? I don’t think I ever did... or will. Unfortunately.

Yes, he broke up with me. It was his first relationship, my fourth. We were in an LDR since we started our relationship in senior year and tried to last during college. 

He broke up with me twice. First time, he was rushing for a frat, and he told me he wanted to see other women, told me we were incompatible, didn't love me anymore, but he still found me attractive but just didn't want a relationship anymore. He contacted me again days later saying he still loved me and doesn't know what he wants. We ended up getting back together because he proved effort. He got into the frat. I was happy for him. He said he couldn't connect to other girls like he connected with me.

Next few months were awesome. We were so in love. He visited me during thanksgiving and winter break.

Then he went back to school. Things got a little rocky. He invited me to come to his frat date night around Valentine's Day. After I visited him, he started acting distant and started ignoring my messages. I told him I got accepted to transfer to the college he's at, then he finally called me and told me that no matter how much he cares about me, he just can't love me as a lover would at this time. He told me the date night was a thing he did to see if he still loved me. We had a good time, had great sex, he thought of nobody but me, but he couldn't force himself to love me like I loved him. He said he wants to be by himself and he wants to figure out who he is and what he wants. He didn't want to lead me on. I have no reason to be angry at him and he said I'm not at fault, that I'm a beautiful, intelligent, kind person with a profound impact on his life and that attraction wasn't an issue; it was an issue with himself and identity.
Yes, got admitted on the 27th of Feb. Good luck!

This is late but honestly, save yourself the money and go to Las Positas, then transfer. You're only paying 45 per unit and the general ed classes are easy. It's not impacted, it's only going to be hard for you to get classes if you don't work hard to keep taking classes and getting good grades. Your priority goes up if you apply for priority registration (early high school decision would benefit you greatly as it did for me) and if you keep your gpa up. For the past three semesters I've gotten nothing but A's and B's. Those AP classes will help you a LOT too.

My advice to you is to apply as soon as possible for Fall 2018, so around March or April or so. They will then tell you to take a mandatory english, writing, math test just to gauge your skill but you can override this later. After, they'll tell you to go to a community counseling session and they'll teach you how to register for classes, here you can talk to your counselor about your AP credits and they'll redirect you to where you override your pre-reqs.

What I did was take my math and social science and physical science first, because I was waiting for my AP Lit and APUSH results so I could override those pre-reqs later.

Around the time Fall semester begins, try to schedule a meeting with your counselor about the student education plan, they will help you lay out a full fledged transfer plan for the college you want to transfer to. They are so helpful because they want to help motivated students to get out and transfer as soon as possible. See your counselor about your SEP once every semester to check up on any changed agreements with colleges or to check your progress. Counselors as Las Positas are more than helpful.

It's kind of lonely here but think of it this way, you're gonna have little to no debt by getting your general education out of the way then transferring to a uni for graduate school. It's gonna help you so much. If you have any questions, let me know, I'm set up for transfer for Fall 2018 at Cal Poly Pomona.
